content:
jordan_engineer: Hey @people-ops — noticed my Feb payroll net pay is about $420 less than usual. Gross looks normal but there is a CT state withholding line on my stub even though my primary residence is MA and I updated my address in ADP months ago. Anyone seen this before?

maria_hr: Thanks for flagging — can you DM me your employee ID so we can pull records? We’ll ping payroll.

jordan_engineer: ID 9742 — sending DM now. Posting here in case it affects others: I was remote in CT for ~2 weeks in Jan but my permanent address has been MA since 2023.

payroll-bot: Payroll run 2026-02-15 processed for batch id pr-20260215-0942. Employee 9742 included in regular run.

ashley_payroll: Looking into this. Quick Q: did you update both ADP (personal info) and the internal HRIS residency flag? We sometimes get a mismatch where ADP updates but internal flag (used for state tax) remains set. Can you paste/redact the payslip lines showing the withholdings?

jordan_engineer: Sure — redacted stub below:

```
Pay period: 02/01/2026 - 02/15/2026
Gross pay: $8,000.00
Federal tax: $1,600.00
FICA: $612.00
CT state tax: $480.00
MA state tax: $0.00
Net pay: $5,308.00
```

ashley_payroll: OK that clarifies. Our system shows CT withholding for that run. It looks like the internal residency flag was set to CT as of 2026-01-18 (probably from your short-term remote entry). ADP address change alone doesn't always flip the residency flag until HR approves the change.

ben_finance: FYI — if earnings were physically performed in CT for part of the period, payroll may withhold CT. But if your tax residency is MA and you didn't trigger CT nonresident withholding, we can reverse withholdings and run an off-cycle correction. Also note W-2s can show multiple state codes if wages were allocated across states.

ashley_payroll: Next steps I propose: (1) We'll run an off-cycle corrective payroll to reverse the CT withholding and apply MA withholding if applicable; (2) HR will update/confirm your residency flag and withholding elections (we'll verify W-4/MA CT forms); (3) We'll issue a correction note and include any tax form guidance if you already filed. If we need to amend a W-2 later we'll handle that in year-end.

maria_hr: Confirming — I've unlocked the residency change workflow for Jordan and will approve MA as primary. Ashley, can you confirm estimated timing for the correction and what the employee will see on the next paystub?

ashley_payroll: I will submit the correction request today (ticket PR-ADJ-6127). Off-cycle typically posts within 7 business days. Expect an adjustment of ~+$420 to net (reversal of CT tax withheld). We'll include a line "Correction: State withholding adjustment (period 02/15/2026)" on the off-cycle stub. If for any reason we can't reverse (e.g., state withholding already remitted), we'll provide instructions for filing an amended return or claim for refund.

jordan_engineer: Appreciate the fast response. Quick question — do I need to file anything with CT personally? I didn't file yet for that period.

ashley_payroll: If we reverse the withholding before CT remittance cutoff (our cutoff is 02/20 for the 02/15 run), you won't need to do anything. If remittance already happened, we'll coordinate a refund/credit path and advise on filing. We'll keep you posted in this thread and update the ticket.

ben_finance: Also flagging for future: teams should use the "temporary remote" field sparingly — it toggles multi-state withholding. Maria, maybe add a short note to the remote policy doc about the residency flag and payroll cutoff dates.

maria_hr: Good call — I'll add a blurb to the HR checklist and ping eng leads.

jordan_engineer: Thank you all — will watch for the off-cycle and confirm when I receive it. :thumbsup:

payroll-bot: Ticket PR-ADJ-6127 created and assigned to ashely_payroll. Estimated completion: 2026-02-24.
